take_homes: Output gets specific because of the context I put in front of the task. Cleverer wording of the prompt isn't what does it.
Put that context in a rules file the agent reads every session, then retro it after real use. The first version is rarely right.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. Use a cold second reader with only the output, and treat self-reports as claims to check.

monday.move: Start a context file for the usage-pricing pilot with the Q2 review as the main source and a note on which sources I distrust. Run the pilot-cohort brief against it, then have a cold reader critique the result.
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team of fourteen
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group meeting
monday.stop_condition: The cold reader finds fewer generic claims than my last manual brief, or I can't tell the two apart and drop it
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: The module says the model didn't improve between Phase 1 and Phase 6 and the context did, and the rules file made that concrete. I still expect prompt craft to matter, but I now think context is the larger share.

one_line: The personal-site exercise was a detour, but the rules file and the cold read are worth having, and I'd cut the module by a third.
